blocks.label: Suppose 90 club respondents give 72 Yes and 10 others give 2 Yes. What is the combined observed proportion?

guided_practice.title: Combine counts
guided_practice.prompt: Group A has 3 Yes of 4 and B has 2 Yes of 6. Find the combined proportion.
guided_practice.answer: 5/10 = 50 percent. The unweighted average of 75 percent and about 33.3 percent is not the combined sample rate.

independent_case.title: Audit independently
independent_case.task: A survey has 18 Yes of 20 club members and 2 Yes of 10 others. Compute both group rates and combined rate. Explain why 20/30 does not automatically describe the whole grade.
independent_case.answer: 90 percent, 20 percent and 20/30 about 66.7 percent. Group sampling proportions and response patterns may differ from the grade.

misconceptions: A successful run proves the conclusion

Group differences suggest that coverage matters, but do not explain why choices differ. Small group counts also make percentages unstable. Use neutral group labels in fictional data rather than personal or sensitive attributes.
Require the new W4 case, explicit predictions and an explanation. Fresh retry: A 6/8 and B 1/2 combine to 7/10 = 70 percent, with group rates 75 and 50 percent. Require a selection limitation.

Surveying another 100 people from the same undercovered source may make the sample larger without fixing the selection problem. Improve access to missing groups and record nonresponse; do not simply duplicate existing rows.

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The combined observed sample has 50 percent Yes. This is not automatically a population estimate: we also need to know how the groups were selected and how many people each represents. Do not average percentages without considering their denominators.

The club has 8 Yes out of 10, and the other group has 2 Yes out of 10. Combine the Yes counts to get 10 and combine the response counts to get 20; the combined observed rate is 10 divided by 20, or 50 percent. When group sizes differ, simply averaging their percentages can give the wrong combined rate. A correct combined calculation still describes the collected sample, not automatically the whole school.
